task: T1: make the resume predicate's gate bound generous, overridable and announced, in `_task_satisfied` in `scripts/ralph-build.sh`. Replace the hardcoded `timeout 60` with a bound read from `RALPH_SATISFIED_TIMEOUT`, in seconds. The FLOOR applies to the DEFAULT and to nothing else: when no usable value is configured, the bound falls back to the loop's own executor bound `RALPH_EXEC_TIMEOUT`. A well-formed override is honoured EXACTLY as given, including values far below that default and including very small ones — clamping an explicit setting up to the default would defeat the only knob this task adds, and a gate proving the bound still bites has to be able to set it to two seconds. The reason the default is that large is that a gate is not permitted to be slower than the work it judges, and a predicate that cannot outwait its own gate has no purpose, which is the whole defect: the same gate runs UNBOUNDED in `run_gates` a few lines away, so the strict bound sits on the cheaper of the two questions. Treat an unset, empty or non-positive-integer value as absent and use the default, never zero — a bound of no time at all would disable resume everywhere while looking like configuration, exactly the failure `HARNESS_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES` is written to avoid. Keep the bound finite: a hanging gate must still fail closed rather than wedge the run, which is why the bound exists and that reason is still good. Then separate the two refusals, which today collapse into one silent `return 1` whose branches are identical: when the gate RAN and did not pass, announce that its gate did not pass; when the gate did not FINISH inside the bound, announce that, naming the bound and how to raise it. Both still return not-satisfied — this changes what a reader is told, never what the predicate decides. Take the verdict from the gate's EXIT STATUS and keep the existing guard that answers not-satisfied on ANY non-zero exit: a failing gate prints a PASS line for every assertion that did hold, so deciding by searching the output for the word PASS reads a red gate as a satisfied task and skips it. That is the one failure mode worse than never skipping — not skipping costs time, this costs correctness and does it silently — and the guard standing in front of it today is the `|| { ... }` on the timeout line, which must survive whatever replaces that line. Announce on the same stream and in the same shape as the other task lines, naming the task, because a task that runs when it should have been skipped is otherwise indistinguishable from a task that was never skippable, and the difference is a bound to raise versus work still to do. Every other uncertain case stays exactly as it is and stays fail-closed: no `tasks/` directory, no gate for the task, a gate that cannot be run, `RALPH_FORCE_ALL`, and `RALPH_FORCE_FROM` at or below this task's index all continue to answer not-satisfied. Do not touch `run_gates`, the attempt loop, the no-op guard, or the skip path's existing announcement, and do not cache, record or read back any verdict — reading a recorded gate result instead of re-running one is a genuine option and belongs to its own spec.
